content.text:
I traced this through the source (`src/run.ts`, `src/thread.ts`, `src/extensions.ts`, `src/durable-extensions.ts`, plus pi-durable 1.5.2 and pit v0.35.1 as installed on this runner). The short answer: **pi-action doesn't load `AGENTS.md` or skills at all.** pi extensions add model providers and nothing else. pi-durable extensions such as pit are the only thing that adds text to the system prompt. With no `extensions` input, the system prompt is empty and the model gets only the tool definitions.

Everything below is laid out for a made-up repo **`acme/xyz`**, checked out at `/home/runner/work/xyz/xyz`, with this config:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    extensions: |
      github:cv/pit#v0.35.1        # pi-durable extension
      ./.pi/extensions/gateway.ts  # pi extension (provider)
```

Someone comments `@pi fix the flaky test` on **xyz issue #12**.

## 1. What each kind of file does in pi-action

| Thing in xyz | Loaded? | Where it ends up |
|---|---|---|
| `xyz/AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` | ❌ never loaded by pi-action | Nowhere, unless the model reads it with `read` or `bash`. Then it's a tool result in the conversation. ([how-it-works.md](docs/how-it-works.md#commit-conventions) says so too.) |
| `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, other `AGENTS.md` files up the directory tree | ❌ | Nowhere |
| Skills (`SKILL.md`, `pi.skills`) | ❌ | Nowhere, not even skill descriptions |
| Prompt templates (`pi.prompts`, for example pit's `./prompts`) | ❌ | Nowhere |
| pi extension (`gateway.ts`, `pi.extensions`) | ✅ at setup | Only `pi.registerProvider()` is used, to add models. Tools, commands, event handlers and UI get a warning in the log and are dropped. |
| pi-durable extension (pit's `pi.durable`) | ✅ at setup | Its **tools** go into the tool list and its **sections** go into the system prompt. If a package has both `pi.durable` and `pi.extensions`, only `pi.durable` is loaded. |
| pit project config (`xyz/.pi/pit.json`, `xyz/.pi/functions`) | Only if `trust_project: true` | The `<pit_project_functions>` section |
| pit user functions (`agent_dir`, by default a fresh `$RUNNER_TEMP/pi-action-agent-*`) | ✅, but the default directory starts empty | The `<pit_user_functions>` section, which is left out while empty |
| The issue, PR diff and review comments | ✅ | The first user message (`buildPrompt`) |

## 2. Timeline of one run

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant GH as GitHub (acme/xyz #12)
    participant PA as pi-action
    participant NPM as $RUNNER_TEMP/pi-action-extensions-*
    participant EXT as Extensions
    participant H as pi-durable Harness
    participant Git as refs/pi/threads/12
    participant M as Model

    GH->>PA: issue_comment "@pi fix the flaky test"
    PA->>GH: getRunContext: check trigger and permissions, fetch issue (and PR diff)
    PA->>GH: react 👀
    rect rgb(240,240,255)
    note over PA,EXT: "Setup" log group (setUp)
    PA->>NPM: npm install --ignore-scripts github:cv/pit#v0.35.1
    PA->>EXT: jiti-load ./.pi/extensions/gateway.ts with a stub pi object
    EXT-->>PA: registerProvider(...) kept, everything else dropped with a warning
    PA->>EXT: jiti-load pit's pi.durable entry (its pi.extensions and prompts are skipped)
    PA->>PA: createActionModels (built-in, custom provider, extension providers)
    PA->>PA: toolEnv: GH_TOKEN and git identity (also put into process.env, because a durable extension is loaded)
    PA->>EXT: createPiDurableExtension({cwd: xyz, agentDir, trustProject, ui, log})
    EXT-->>PA: pit = { tools: [typescript], sections: [...] }
    end
    PA->>Git: fetch thread ref
    PA->>H: registry.install(coding-tools), then registry.install(pit)
    PA->>H: Harness.open, root.configure({model, cwd})
    opt continuing thread with a working-tree snapshot
        PA->>H: write user message "[pi-action] Restored working-tree snapshot..."
    end
    PA->>H: submit(first message, or follow-up with reply reminder)
    H->>EXT: render sections (each request, in the "prepare" phase)
    H->>H: write pi.system entry (full prompt the first time, only changes after that)
    H->>M: [system + tools] + transcript
    M-->>H: tool calls (it may read AGENTS.md now, as a normal file)
    H->>Git: commit entries, push at turn boundaries
    loop every poll_interval
        PA->>GH: new @pi comments?
        PA->>H: submit(whenBusy: "steer"): joins the running conversation
    end
    M-->>H: final text
    PA->>GH: post comment, react 🚀
    PA->>Git: close and push
```

Three timing details:

- **Extensions are loaded on every run.** The thread stored in git doesn't record which extensions were installed. If you change `extensions:` between runs, the next request on the same thread gets a different tool list.
- **Sections are rendered again before every model request.** pi-durable compares the result with what the model has already seen. If something changed (for example, pit saved a function or set a note), it adds a `pi.system` entry with only the change. That entry sits at its place in the conversation and is not rewritten at the top.
- **The system message is moved to the front.** The first user message is stored before the system prompt is first rendered. When the request is built, `leadWithSystem` moves that first system message ahead of it, so providers treat it as the initial prompt and the prompt cache stays valid.

## 3. What the context window looks like

### First request on a new thread (xyz #12)

```mermaid
block-beta
  columns 1
  block:sys["SYSTEM (one message, sections joined with blank lines)"]
    columns 1
    s0["content: '' (pi-action and pi-durable add no base prompt)"]
    s1["<pit_guidelines> how to use the typescript tool"]
    s2["<pit_tools> host tools reachable as tools.* (read, write, edit, bash)"]
    s3["<pit_user_functions> (left out while empty)"]
    s4["<pit_project_functions> (only with trust_project and xyz/.pi/functions)"]
    s5["<pit_notes> (left out until pit sets a note)"]
  end
  tools["TOOLS: read, write, edit, bash (coding-tools), then typescript (pit)"]
  u1["USER: # GitHub Issue #12 / Title / Description / Task / Your Reply / Artifact requirements (PR: review comments, PR Diff)"]
  a1["ASSISTANT / TOOL RESULTS ... (for example read xyz/AGENTS.md, which arrives here as a tool result)"]
```

### A later run on the same thread (`@pi also update the docs`)

```
┌ SYSTEM            baseline sections and tools (replayed from refs/pi/threads/12)
├ USER              # GitHub Issue #12 ... (first run)
├ ASSISTANT/TOOLS   ... first run's work ...
├ ASSISTANT         first reply
├ SYSTEM (update)   "Updated system prompt section pit_notes: ..." (only if a section changed)
├ USER              [pi-action] Restored working-tree snapshot ... (only with worktree snapshots)
├ USER              **@alice** commented (https://github.com/acme/xyz/issues/12#issuecomment-…):
│                   also update the docs
│                   (pi-action posts your final response as a comment here. Don't also post it with `gh`.)
└ ASSISTANT/TOOLS   ...
```

The issue body and diff are **not** sent again on follow-ups. When the context gets too big, pi-durable compaction replaces older history with a summary. The system sections are rendered again after that.

### Without the `extensions` input

The SYSTEM block is **empty**. The model gets only the four tool definitions and the user message, with no guidance, `AGENTS.md`, or skills.

## 4. How this differs from pi's own coding agent (CLI)

As I understand pi's CLI, it puts its base prompt, the `AGENTS.md` files (global and up the directory tree), and the skill descriptions into the system prompt, and runs extension tools and commands. pi-action does none of this. It relies on the model choosing to read `xyz/AGENTS.md`, which the built-in prompt doesn't even ask it to do. To have it loaded every time, you could add `AGENTS.md` to the system prompt as a pi-durable section (inside pi-action, or as a small extension), or add "read AGENTS.md first" to `prompt_template` (first message only). I can open a follow-up issue for either.

This was a question, so I didn't change or commit any files.
